reason: Both treat moving in step with the world as the test of understanding, which those who never learn it lack, however much else they learn.

quotes.838: it is like a madman getting drunk
quotes.977: when it falls to the unworthy, turns to nothing but excess

reason: Both show gain unhinging a small mind: the fool is a madman getting drunk, and distinction in the unworthy turns to nothing but excess.

quotes.115: Loss and gain will always come
quotes.210: ruin is rare for anyone who doesn’t stray aside to do evil

reason: Loss will always come, whatever your heart does, yet ruin is said to be rare for anyone who doesn’t stray aside to do evil.

quotes.155: Those who bear it are wrapped up and kept like gold
quotes.880: Those who fail to crush the pride of their foes surely won’t live

reason: Those who punish a wrong count for nothing and those who bear it are kept like gold, yet those who don’t crush their foes’ pride won’t live to draw breath.

quotes.182: to ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely to their face
quotes.829: make them laugh, and within that friendship hold them so that it dies

reason: Smiling falsely to a face while ruining behind the back is worse than doing wrong, yet it is the advice for those who make much of you and despise you.

quotes.222: Even if it were a good road, taking is bad

reason: Taking is bad even if it were a good road, yet to beg from those who hide nothing is called like giving.

quotes.292: Even a lie counts as truthfulness, if it brings good with no fault in it
quotes.656: Even if you see the mother who bore you go hungry, don’t do what the worthy condemn

reason: A lie counts as truthfulness if it brings good, yet what the worthy condemn stays forbidden even when the mother who bore you goes hungry.

quotes.321: Killing brings with it every action of the other kind
quotes.771: Many have stood before him, and now they stand in stone

reason: Killing brings every wrong with it, says one; in the other, the many his lord has killed, now standing in stone, are a warrior’s boast.

remove: “Two roads to a full life” was the old framing. K342 says nothing of wealth and K760 nothing of renouncing, so they don’t really pull.

quotes.373: the understanding you were born with still wins out
quotes.452: People’s understanding takes on the nature of their company

reason: The understanding you were born with wins out over all your study, yet people’s understanding is also said to take on the nature of their company.

quotes.376: What isn’t yours by fate won’t stay, however hard you guard it
quotes.482: a rope that ties good fortune down so that it can’t leave

reason: What fate denies won’t stay however you guard it, yet acting in step with the season is a rope that ties good fortune down.

quotes.380: Even as you plan a way around it, it gets there first
quotes.666: Those who plan will get what they planned, just as they planned it, if they are firm

reason: Fate gets there first even as you plan around it, yet those who plan are said to get just what they planned, if they are firm.

quotes.476: Those who have climbed to the tip of a branch and try to go further will lose their life
quotes.596: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher

reason: Climbing past the tip of a branch costs your life, yet all your thoughts are to be of rising higher, since even failing has the nature of not failing.

quotes.1282: you must not sulk even by a millet seed
quotes.1330: Sulking is the joy of desire

reason: Full desire leaves no room for a millet seed of sulking, yet sulking is called the joy of desire.

quotes.154: guard your patience and live by it
quotes.301: Whoever holds back anger where it can take effect truly holds it back

reason: Patience may keep your integrity with you, but holding back anger only counts where the anger could take effect.

quotes.468: Effort not made the right way will crack
quotes.620: Those who strive without faltering and without delay will see the back of fate itself

reason: Striving may see the back of fate, but only if it is made the right way: effort that isn’t will crack, however many stand guard.

quotes.534: There is no fort for those who are afraid
quotes.741: of value to those who fear and look after themselves

reason: A fortress serves those who fear and look after themselves, but for those who are only afraid there is no fort at all.

quotes.549: punish wrongdoing is no stain on a ruler
quotes.561: looks into a wrong fairly and punishes to fit it

reason: Punishing wrongdoing is no stain on a ruler and is his work, but he must look into the wrong fairly and punish to fit it.

quotes.391: Once you have learned it, live up to it
quotes.637: Even when you know the methods, know the nature of the world and then act

reason: Living up to what you have learned isn’t the end of it: even when you know the methods, you must know the nature of the world before you act.

quotes.238: it is a disgrace for everyone on earth not to gain the legacy called renown
quotes.962: won’t do anything unworthy, even for glory

reason: Gaining renown is a duty, but not at any price: those who want glory with strength of character won’t do anything unworthy even for it.

quotes.368: Those without craving have no suffering
quotes.1036: If those who plough fold their hands, even those who say they have given up all desire can’t stand firm

reason: Having no craving is no guarantee against suffering: if those who plough fold their hands, even those who have given up all desire can’t stand firm.

quotes.1302: A sulk is like the right amount of salt. Drawing it out is like a little too much
quotes.1326: a quarrel is sweeter than making love

reason: A quarrel may be sweeter than making love, but only in the right amount: drawn out, a sulk is like a little too much salt.

quotes.26: Those who do what is hard to do are great
quotes.975: The great will carry out hard deeds

reason: Greatness is defined the same way in both: the great are those who do what is hard to do.

quotes.36: Don’t say “I’ll see to it some other day.”
quotes.335: Before your tongue is stilled and the hiccup rises, rush to do good deeds

quotes.88: After anxious guarding they will say “We have nothing to hold on to”
quotes.1001: He stores up great heaps of wealth and doesn’t eat from it. He is a dead man

reason: Wealth guarded and never used comes to nothing: the hoarder ends with nothing to hold on to, or as a dead man beside it.

quotes.113: let go at once of gain that comes from leaving the middle
quotes.657: Better the deep poverty of the worthy than prosperity gained by wearing disgrace

quotes.170: No one has grown great through envy

quotes.140: may learn much, but they are still without understanding
quotes.834: No one is a greater fool than someone who studies, understands, teaches others, and still has no self-control

reason: Learning doesn’t cure folly: much learning can leave you without understanding, and the greatest fool of all is a teacher with no self-control.

quotes.158: Defeat by your own worth those who wrong you
quotes.985: That is the weapon the worthy use to turn enemies around

reason: Worth is the way to beat an enemy: defeat those who wrong you by your own worth, and bowing is the weapon the worthy use to turn enemies around.

quotes.218: Even when they have little room to give, those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping others
quotes.955: Even when what they have to give has shrunk, those of an old family don’t part from their good nature

reason: Goodness outlasts the means for it: those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping, and old families keep their good nature as their giving shrinks.

quotes.386: If a ruler is easy to see and not harsh in speech, his land will be praised above all others
quotes.548: A ruler who isn’t easy to reach, and doesn’t look into things and give justice, will sink low and fall by himself

reason: Being easy to reach decides how a ruler stands: with it his land is praised above all others, without it he falls by himself.

quotes.389: a ruler with the character to bear words bitter to his ears
quotes.448: A ruler with no one to rebuke him has no protection

reason: A ruler lasts by bearing what stings: the world rests under one who bears bitter words, and one with no one to rebuke him falls.

quotes.461: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained, and the profit it will bring later, then act
quotes.676: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain you will reach when it is done, and then act

reason: One rule of action stated twice: weigh the cost, the obstacles and the gain to come, and only then act.

quotes.465: To march out without thinking through every side of it
quotes.491: Start nothing and scorn no one until you have found the ground for a siege

reason: No war should begin before it is prepared for: think through every side of it first, and find the ground for a siege first.

quotes.555: are they not the weapon that wears away wealth?
quotes.659: All that was taken with tears leaves with tears

reason: What is gained through others’ tears is lost to tears: the tears of those who suffer wear away wealth, and what was taken with tears leaves with tears.

quotes.571: This world exists because of the surpassing beauty called kindly regard
quotes.996: The world goes on because of the courteous

reason: The world keeps going only because of gentle ways, called kindly regard in one and courtesy in the other.

quotes.706: the face shows what is strongest in the heart
quotes.1273: Like the thread that shows through a bead, something shows through this young woman’s adornment

reason: What lies within shows through: the heart in the face, as crystal shows what is beside it, and something in her adornment, like a thread through a bead.

quotes.719: don’t speak in a petty one, even by forgetting
quotes.849: Whoever tries to show a man who can’t see ends up seeing nothing himself

reason: Good speech is wasted on the petty: don’t speak there even by forgetting, since trying to show a man who can’t see leaves you seeing nothing.

quotes.961: Even things you can’t do without, give them up if they would lower you
quotes.1017: They won’t give up shame for life

quotes.988: Having nothing is no disgrace, if you have the strength called worth
quotes.1047: looked at as a stranger, even by the mother who bore him

reason: Goodness decides what poverty does: with worth there is no disgrace, without righteousness a man is a stranger even to the mother who bore him.

quotes.1152: Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave
quotes.1276: He comforts me so fully and joins me so gladly, but in it I see myself bearing pain again

quotes.1152: Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave
quotes.1295: when it has him it fears parting

quotes.1157: Won’t these bangles slipping from my forearm spread the word
quotes.1235: Your arms, their bangles gone and their old beauty withered, tell of the cruelty of a cruel man

reason: Her slipped bangles do the telling: what her arms have lost tells everyone that he has gone, and how cruel he is.
